prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Sign In to Restore Your Saved Desktop Pets", "Logging into your account automatically syncs and recovers all previously adopted desktop companions."]
1: ["Create Your Custom Pet", "Follow the step-by-step preview to generate your custom pet accurately."]
2: ["Access Your Pet Account", "Sign in to keep your pet data safe and synchronized across all your desktop devices."]
3: ["Use bright, clear front-facing photos for the most accurate custom pet generation."]
4: ["How to Control & Interact With Your Desktop Pet", "Right-click your pet to open quick actions, drag to move across your screen, or double-click to chat anytime."]
5: ["Review Custom Pet Features", "Verify Your Pet's Appearance", "Confirm your pet preview looks correct before generating your adoption certificate.", "Looks Great!"]
6: ["Choose Your Adoption Path", "Select a quick pre-made companion or create a custom pet tailored to you."]
7: ["Signing in links your pet securely to your cloud profile so your companion is never lost."]
8: ["Preparing Desktop Engine", "Your pet is getting ready to land on your desktop display."]
9: ["Tip: Access settings or hide your pet anytime from the system tray icon in your taskbar."]

verdicts.problem: Asks for personal photos of the user.
